title: Nocturne of Shadow
hook: Complete ocarina line of the duet: B-A-A-D-B-A-F (the in-game ocarina song), a rest while the strings answer, then G#-F#-F#-C#-G#-F# and the closing F

evidence.level: two-MIDI exact pitch/onset comparison of the dedicated ocarina tracks, a third sequence, the decompiled game note table and the official Nintendo score for the seven in-game notes, and an inspection of the original recording
evidence.summary: VGMusic nocturneofshadow.mid (Graeme Stewart) track 1 (ocarina, program 79; the whole 14-note line, no overlaps) events 0-13 (80 BPM, exact grid) vs Z5NocturneOfShadow.mid (Eddie1989) track 7 (ocarina, program 79; the whole track) events 0-13 (95 BPM): 14 pitches and metrical attacks identical. Both files give the answer G-F-F-C-G-F, four beats before the sequence, to another instrument (strings an octave lower in the primary), so it is not part of the ocarina line. bitmidi 112979, a flute reduction in octave pairs, has the same 14 events (upper notes, the answer skipped) within 0.025391 beat. zeldaret/oot 14759ab sOcarinaSongNotes[OCARINA_SONG_NOCTURNE] decodes B4 A4 A4 D4 B4 A4 F4 (+12 = MIDI B5 A5 A5 D5 B5 A5 F5) at 36/33(+1)/(3 rest)/18/18/18/18/144 frames (a quarter is 36 frames): attacks within 1 frame. Nintendo's official score of the song (4/4: two quarters, four eighths, a dotted half) has the same seven pitches and attacks. The table and the score hold only the seven in-game notes; events 7-13 rest on the MIDIs. Original recording (attributed soundtrack upload, inspection only): the expected pitch is the strongest semitone in 13 of 14 note windows and the second strongest in the other (the D5, the quietest note of the game table).

corpus.notes: Attributed soundtrack upload, 5-20 s of a 21 s track: the ocarina phrase without the opening harp statement. Inspected per note window only; upload identity and note-level alignment are not validated. The recording runs at about 90 BPM with a closing ritardando; the arrangement keeps the 80 BPM of the primary.
